history.period: 1988 (death of Om Singh Rathore) - shrine built in the 1990s (verify); legend sources disagree on the date: 2 Dec 1988 vs 5 May 1988 (verify)
history.summary: FOLK/MODERN SHRINE (not a traditional temple) - KEEP-OR-DROP DECISION NEEDED. CSV TOWN FLAG: the shrine is NOT in Pali town - it stands at Chotila village on the Pali-Jodhpur highway (NH-62), roughly 20 km from Pali and 50-70 km from Jodhpur, in Pali district. Documented with the corrected location. Om Banna (Om Singh Rathore, son of Thakur Jog Singh Rathore of Chotila) was travelling from Bangdi near Sanderao to Chotila when his motorcycle hit a tree and he was killed (1988). Police twice took the bike to the station, emptying its fuel tank and chaining it, but each morning it was found back at the accident spot. Locals took this as a miracle and built a shrine where the bike is worshipped; devotees - mostly truck and taxi drivers - stop for safe-journey blessings and offer bangles, scarves, sweets and flowers on the tree at the spot. Poonam Giri has served as priest/maintainer for two decades per visitor reports (verify). Coordinates are APPROXIMATE (district-level geocode of Chotila).

name: Om Banna Temple (Bullet Baba)
town: Chotila (CSV town 'Pali' is the district, not the location - the shrine is at Chotila village on the Pali-Jodhpur highway)
town_description: Chotila is a small village on the Pali-Jodhpur highway (NH-62) in Pali district, about 20 km from Pali town and 50-70 km from Jodhpur. The shrine is a roadside stop, not a town temple; visitors typically halt for 3-5 minutes while driving between Jodhpur and Pali/Ranakpur.

travel.road: On NH-62 between Pali and Jodhpur at Chotila village; a roadside halt, not a destination (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: September to March, daytime; it is a highway halt rather than a day-trip destination.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Open through the day (roadside shrine - verify).
